summary: The main article describes a diastereoselective and enantioselective photoredox pinacol coupling of aromatic aldehydes using titanium complexes and a red-absorbing organic dye. It includes optimization tables for reaction conditions, scope schemes for both racemic and enantioselective variants, and mechanistic studies including photophysical data and non-linear effect analysis.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: (A) Use of organic red-absorbing dye [ n Pr-DMQA] + [BF4] 1 [BF4] 0 in palldium mediated metallaphotoredox catalysis; (B) this work: photoredox pinacol coupling promoted by titanium complexes with a redabsorbing organic dye.
items.description: This figure compares previous work using the DMQA dye in palladium catalysis with the current work involving titanium-mediated photoredox pinacol coupling.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the pinacol coupling reaction mediated by Cp2TiCl2
items.description: This table details the optimization of reaction conditions, including photocatalyst screening, solvent effects, and control experiments for the pinacol coupling of p-chlorobenzaldehyde.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Scope of the diastereoselective pinacol coupling promoted by Cp2TiCl2.
items.description: This scheme illustrates the substrate scope for the diastereoselective pinacol coupling of various aromatic aldehydes using Cp2TiCl2.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Optimization of the pinacol coupling reaction mediated by chiral titanium complexes
items.description: This table presents the optimization of the enantioselective variant of the reaction using chiral SalenTiCl2 complexes.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of the enantioselective photoredox pinacol coupling with ( R , R )-SalenTiCl2.
items.description: This scheme shows the scope of the enantioselective pinacol coupling for different aromatic aldehydes, providing yields, diastereomeric ratios, and enantiomeric ratios.

items.caption: (A) Absorption (blue line) and fl uorescence spectra (red line) of a PhCF3 solution of 4 + (31 m M) at r. t. ( l ex ¼ 575 nm). (B) Comparison between fl uorescence decays of air-equilibrated (blue dots) and N2saturated (red dots) PhCF3 solutions of 4 + ( ca. 30 m M) at r.t.
items.description: This figure displays the photophysical properties of the organic dye photocatalyst, including absorption, fluorescence, and lifetime measurements.

items.caption: Mechanistic proposal for the photoredox pinacol coupling catalyzed by 4 + in the presence of titanium complexes ( A ) and by TADF dye 7 ( B ).
items.description: This figure outlines the proposed catalytic cycles for the stereoselective titanium-mediated process versus the non-selective direct photoredox process.

items.description: This graph shows the non-linear effect study, plotting product enantiomeric excess against catalyst enantiomeric excess to investigate the bimetallic nature of the mechanism.
